messages:
maria: Quick callout — ran a 6h profile sweep on prod and noticed token-level latency spikes on two routes (/chat, /embed). p50 ~8ms but p95 jumps to ~220ms and p99 hits ~900ms in short bursts. Spikes correlate with kernel switches + KV miss bursts. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/_abc123/token-breakdown
jon: can you paste the exact query and the time window you used?
sasha: fwiw that pattern smells like kernel-selection thrash + cold KV cache. probably a sequencing where batching chooses a kernel, then a different kernel warms up and we see cache miss cascades.
maria: query I ran (PromQL):
```
sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[1m])) by (route, kernel)

# also looked at: increase(kv_miss_total[5m]) / increase(kv_req_total[5m])
```
window = 6h, aligned to deploys. spikes start ~1880119800 and recur every ~20-40s for ~5m.
ana: @maria can you also screenshot the per-route batching size distribution? want to see if small batches correlate.
maria: attaching quick clip in dash — /chat shows median batch=1.8, tail > 8 during spikes. /embed stays at median 4 but drops to 1 during the same bursts.
kevin: hypotheses: 1) batching heuristic backoff on perceived latency (so batches shrink), 2) kernel pivot thresholds are oscillating (seq_len boundary), 3) KV TTL eviction pattern when an alternative kernel warms caches.
jon: on alerting side — our burn rate calc is token_latency_burnrate = sum(latency > slo)/slo over 5m. right now we only alert cluster-wide; we should add per-route burn rate and a short-window anomaly detector.
sasha: Agree. Also propose adding a kernel-selection metric: kernel_switch_count{route,kernel_from,kernel_to}. That would make the correlation explicit.
nana: I'd add a KV-hit-window metric: kv_hit_ratio_1m_by_route and a smoothing window to avoid paging on short bursts. set paging threshold to sustained >30s.
oncall-bot: Paging rule: latency_burnrate > 3 for 5m on any route -> page oncall. Current rule is cluster-only, will cause noisy pages.
maria: For next steps I'm proposing an experiment:
- Add per-route burn-rate alert with a 10m cooldown and 90s grace to prevent short spikes from paging.
- Add kernel_switch_count telemetry and per-kernel token p95.
- Tune batching: raise max batching latency cap from 15ms -> 30ms for /chat to let batches accumulate.
- Increase KV soft-ttl for those hot prefixes from 60s -> 300s as a canary.
- Run canary A/B (10% traffic) with kernel pivot at seq_len 256 instead of 512.
kevin: I can implement the batching cap and kernel pivot in a canary config this afternoon. will add feature flag.
jon: I'll own the alerts — will create a per-route burnrate SLO dashboard + Datadog anomaly monitor (metric: per_route_token_p95) and set notify: infra and oncall with a 10m suppression window for identical signals.
sasha: For instrumentation PR, include a lightweight sample emitter in runtime that tags requests with kernel_hint and batch_id. this will make trace->metric joins easier. small perf cost.
nana: Sounds good. Also let's not forget to add a short-term circuit: if kernel_switch_count_rate > X then fallback to stable-kernel variant for that route for 30s. avoids thrash.
infra-bot: k8s-autoscaler triggered scale up: deployment/runtime-gpu +2 pods at 1880123540 (auto-scaling based on gpu_util).
oncall-bot: noted. will lower page severity to P2 for the next 2 hours while we run canary.
maria: I'll open the PRs: instrumentation + canary config + alert changes. tagging @kevin for canary rollout and @jon for alert creation.
kevin: ack, starting work now.
jon: ack, I'll draft the monitors and add runbook entries: "If per-route burnrate > 2 for >10m, check kernel_switch_count and kv_hit_ratio. Toggle batching cap/ttl A/B if needed."
sasha: thanks team. looking to re-evaluate after 6h canary. if noise persists, we may need deeper kernel-selection invariants (avoid oscillation within 1min window). :eyes:
